bd_president_lineup.d: After two games without a win the chairman calls you: he would like to see the players he wanted in the summer on the pitch.

o.r: The chairman is pleased. The dressing room, though, has seen who really is in charge.
The chairman appreciates the clarity and lets you get on with it.
o.rb: The chairman takes it as an insult and lets everyone know.

o.l: Tell him I pick the team
o.r: The players see you standing up for them. The boardroom is far less happy.

bd_budget_cut.d: The accounts are in the red: the club has to cut the transfer budget and asks for your cooperation.

o.r: The budget drops by a third, but the club sees you as a company man.
You win them over: the cut is minimal.
o.rb: The tug of war annoys the board: the cut will be even bigger.

o.r: The cut is smaller, but the fans protest about the prices.

bd_sponsor_betting.d: A betting company offers a lucrative deal to appear on the training kit. The chairman wants your opinion.

o.r: The budget grows, but some fans don’t like it.

o.l: Oppose it: it’s not the club’s image
o.r: The fans applaud you. Some in the boardroom think the money was needed.
A compromise that bothers few people and brings in something.

bd_stadium_works.d: The club wants to relay the pitch and rebuild a stand mid-season: for a month the team will play on an uneven surface.

o.r: The fans love the new stadium; for a few matches the ball bounces badly.
It’s postponed: some fans moan about yet another delay.

bd_sporting_director.t: The sporting director works against you
bd_sporting_director.d: Word from the offices: the sporting director badmouths your work to the chairman and pushes for another manager.

o.r: You avoid the clash. But the staff see you won’t stand your ground.

o.l: Ask for a three-way meeting with the chairman
o.r: The meeting strengthens you: the director backs off.
o.rb: The chairman sides with the director: you are more isolated than before.

bd_contract_extension.t: The chairman wants to tie you down
bd_contract_extension.d: Things are going well: the chairman offers you a new contract before the end of the season.

o.r: Contract signed: the club sees you as its manager for years to come.
The chairman agrees: more money for transfers.
o.rb: The demand goes down badly: the new deal stays in the drawer.

o.r: Your reputation grows, but the chairman feels kept waiting.

bd_preseason_tour.d: The marketing department has organised a summer tour on the other side of the world: big revenue, long flights.

o.r: The tour brings money and visibility. The team comes back tired.

o.l: A mountain training camp, old school
o.r: No extra money, but the team works on fitness and on its game.

bd_analyst_hire.d: The club can hire an analyst from a big team: video, data, reports on the opponents.

o.r: The staff are better prepared: your assistant’s advice will be sharper and youth estimates more accurate.

o.l: I prefer work on the pitch
o.r: The usual methods continue.

bd_assistant_leaves.d: Your assistant has been offered a head coach job at a smaller club.

o.l: Let him go with a hug
o.r: He leaves with your blessing. His replacement will take a while to settle in.

o.l: Ask the club to give him a raise
o.r: He stays, happy to have been kept.

bd_owner_style.d: The owners ask you to play more attacking football: they say the crowd is bored, and so are the sponsors.

o.r: Owners and fans are happy. The team will have to relearn a lot.
The owners trust your method.
o.rb: The owners aren’t convinced and will hold it against you at the first defeat.

bd_takeover_rumours.d: A rumour says a foreign fund is ready to buy the club. Journalists ask you what you think.

o.l: No comment: I’m focused on the team
o.r: A professional answer, but the uncertainty weighs on the group.

o.l: Say new owners would do the club good
o.r: The fans like it. The current chairman, much less.

bd_training_ground.d: The training centre is old: worn pitches, a small gym. Rebuilding it costs part of the transfer budget.

o.r: New facilities: better work, and the youngsters develop faster.
The club appreciates the caution.

bd_academy_funds.d: The head of the academy asks for funds for new scouts and coaches. Results would show in a few years.

o.l: Yes, the future is built now
o.r: The academy gets stronger: from next summer better youngsters will come through.
The academy stays as it is.

bd_ultimatum_meeting.d: The board summons you: results aren’t coming and they want to know what you plan to do.

o.r: The plan convinces them: the board gives you time.
o.rb: The plan convinces nobody: the atmosphere gets heavy.

o.r: The board likes it, but the players are unsettled by the changes.

o.l: Defend the players: the football is there, luck isn’t
o.r: The team rallies around you. The board less so.

bd_bonus_dispute.d: The senior players want bigger win bonuses. The club says the budget won’t allow it and asks you to mediate.

o.l: Side with the players: pay the bonuses
o.r: The club pays, the players are fired up.
The club thanks you. The dressing room feels betrayed.

o.l: Propose bonuses tied to the season target
o.r: Compromise accepted by everyone.
o.rb: The proposal pleases nobody.

bd_kit_launch.d: The kit supplier wants the whole squad at the launch of the new shirt, in the town square, the day before an important session.

o.r: A great party, shirt sales through the roof.
A low-key event: the sponsor and the fans are disappointed.

bd_goalkeeper_coach.d: A famous former goalkeeper offers himself as goalkeeping coach. He’s expensive, but his methods are renowned.

o.r: The keepers work better from the first week.

o.l: The one we have is fine
o.r: No change to the staff.

bd_physio_conflict.d: Three players out at once: the fitness coach blames the medical staff and vice versa.

o.r: New methods and lighter workloads: the team breathes again. Some grumbling among the staff.
The staff stay together, but the workloads stay heavy.

bd_scout_network.d: The sporting director proposes opening a scouting network in South America and Africa.

o.r: More eyes around the world: player reports become more accurate.
The current scouts stay.

bd_ticket_prices.d: The stadium is half empty. Your captain asks you to persuade the club to sell cheap tickets.

o.r: A full, loud stadium in the following matches. Less revenue.
Prices stay high. The fans keep staying away.

bd_president_interview.t: The chairman talks to the papers
bd_president_interview.d: In an interview the chairman says “the manager is not under discussion, for now”. That “for now” makes every paper.

o.l: Reply that he’s right to demand more
o.r: The humble answer calms things, but makes you look weak.

o.l: Reply that he could have spared us the “for now”
o.r: The answer lands well: a manager with character.
o.rb: The chairman is furious: the rift is now public.

bd_women_team.d: The club asks your staff to share the training ground and some methods with the women’s team.

o.r: A fine collaboration: the club’s image improves.
Each goes their own way.

bd_financial_fair_play.d: The federation opens an investigation into the club’s accounts: transfer limits could follow.

o.r: No sanctions, but the budget shrinks a lot.
The appeal works: almost no consequences.
o.rb: The appeal makes it worse: a heavy sanction and bad press.

bd_captain_board.d: {player} publicly criticised the club over how it treats players. The chairman wants you to take away his armband.

o.r: The club likes the firmness. {player} won’t forgive you easily.
The dressing room is with you. The chairman won’t forget it.

bd_youth_quota.d: The club asks you to play {player}, one of the academy talents: they want to raise his value.

o.r: The club is satisfied. Now those two starts really have to happen.
A consistent choice, but the club wanted a different answer.

bd_bus_breakdown.d: The night before the away trip the team coach breaks down: you risk reaching the hotel in the middle of the night.

o.r: You arrive at two in the morning: the team barely sleeps.
It costs a bit, but the team arrives rested and in good spirits.

bd_president_son.d: The chairman asks you to let his nephew train with the first team: a seventeen-year-old talent, “according to him”.

o.r: The chairman is happy. The players snigger.

o.l: He has to go through the youth team first
o.r: The right answer. The chairman is still hurt.

bd_naming_rights.d: A company offers a lot of money to put its name on the historic stadium. The fans are alarmed.

o.r: A big sum arrives. The fans will never call the stadium by its new name.

o.l: The stadium stays as it is
o.r: The fans adore you. The club reluctantly gives up the money.

bd_pitch_invasion_fine.d: After the win some fans ran onto the pitch to celebrate. A hefty fine arrives.

o.l: The club pays and moves on
o.r: The fans appreciate that the club didn’t turn on them.

o.l: Ask the club to identify those responsible
o.r: A hard line: the board approves, the ultras don’t.

bd_loan_policy.d: The sporting director wants to loan out, for a fee, the youngsters who hardly play: money in and minutes for them.

o.r: Some money in and minutes for the kids elsewhere. A few didn’t want to go.

o.l: I want to keep them here training with me
o.r: The youngsters stay and feel valued.

bd_medical_tech.d: The medical staff ask for a cryo-chamber and GPS sensors to monitor workloads.

o.r: The team recovers better between matches.

o.l: We recover the way we always have
o.r: No extra spending.

bd_friendly_money.d: During the international break an invitation arrives for a friendly abroad with a big appearance fee.

o.r: The budget grows, the legs are a little less fresh.
The team recharges.

bd_social_media_team.d: The communications office wants to film behind-the-scenes content, including in the dressing room before matches.

o.l: Fine, the fans will love it
o.r: The videos go viral. Some players feel watched, though.
The players appreciate the privacy.

bd_documentary.d: A streaming platform wants to follow the team all season and turn it into a series.

o.r: Money and fame: everyone will know your methods. But the cameras never switch off.
Work continues away from the spotlight.

bd_documentary_scene.d: The cameras caught your half-time rant. The producers want it in the first episode.

o.r: The scene goes viral: you look like a real manager. Some players feel exposed.

o.l: Pay the penalty to cut it
o.r: The scene disappears, and some money with it.

bd_ceo_budget_bonus.d: The season is going beyond expectations: the club wants to reward you. You can choose how.

o.l: More budget for the January window
o.r: The club increases the budget.

o.l: A team dinner and a bonus for the players
o.r: The squad celebrates: the atmosphere is superb.

bd_travel_policy.d: For long away trips the staff ask for charter flights instead of scheduled flights with layovers.

o.r: Shorter journeys, fresher team.
A few more hours in airports, a few more euros in the bank.

bd_nutritionist_chef.d: The nutritionist wants to change the canteen menu: no pasta at lunch, only measured meals.

o.r: The players grumble, but the fitness tests improve.
The players are grateful.

bd_referee_complaint.d: After the defeat the chairman wants you to attack the referee at the press conference: “Say what you think”.

o.r: The fans cheer. The disciplinary judge bans you for one match.
A classy answer: you earn respect, but the fans wanted blood.

bd_old_legend_role.t: A club legend on the staff
bd_old_legend_role.d: The club wants to add an old club legend to your staff: adored by fans, but no coaching experience.

o.r: The fans are thrilled and the dressing room listens to him. Technically he helps little.
A professional choice. The fans see it as a snub.

bd_pitch_winter.d: The cold has frozen the home pitch: the ball won’t roll. The groundsman proposes emergency pitch heating.

o.r: The pitch is playable again: you can play your own game.
Heavy pitch: less passing, more long balls.

bd_agent_influence.d: An agent very close to the chairman offers three mediocre players at high prices. The chairman “suggests” signing one.

o.l: Sign one to keep the peace
o.r: The chairman is happy. A useless player in the squad and money wasted.
You said no to the chairman’s friend: your independence makes the news.

bd_away_fans_trip.d: For the next away game the club can provide coaches for the fans. The captain says having them close would make a difference.

o.l: The club pays for the coaches
o.r: The away end is packed: the team feels the push.
A half-empty away end.

bd_ethics_code.d: The club wants to introduce a code of conduct: curfew, no social media after 10pm, hefty fines.

o.r: More discipline and more rest. Some players feel treated like kids.
The dressing room appreciates the trust.

bd_president_dinner.d: The chairman invites you to dinner with the sponsors the night before a closed training session.

o.r: A useful evening: the chairman introduces you as his trusted man.
The chairman understands, but he’s hurt.

bd_budget_bonus_winter.d: The club has closed a good commercial deal: it asks if you want to use the money in the window or save it.

o.l: In the window: we need reinforcements
o.r: Budget increased for the January window.
The club appreciates the caution.

bd_video_room.d: Your assistant proposes an hour of video every day to study the movements of your system.

o.r: The team grasps the system faster.
More pitch, less theory.

ch_painkiller_star.d: {player} has a hamstring niggle. The doctor says he can play with injections, but there is a risk.

o.r: {player} grits his teeth and plays.
{player} skips training and recovers. He isn’t happy.

ch_painkiller_after.d: {player} has been playing through pain for weeks. The medical staff ask whether to carry on.

o.l: One more match, then we’ll see
o.r: The pain eases: {player} is in form and grateful.
o.rb: The hamstring gives way: {player} is out for over a month.

o.r: {player} stops in time. He loses a little rhythm.

ch_referee_rant.d: {club} lost to a very dubious penalty. The microphones are on.

o.l: Attack the referee without mincing words
o.r: The dressing room and fans are with you. The disciplinary committee takes note.
A gentleman’s answer. Some in the dressing room wanted more fight.

ch_referee_hearing.d: Your words about the referee have reached the disciplinary judge. You can defend yourself or apologise.

o.l: Defend myself: I told the truth
o.r: The judge drops the case: no sanction.
o.rb: A one-match touchline ban and a fine: your assistant will be on the bench.

o.r: No ban. Your image takes a slight knock.

ch_teen_agent.d: {player}’s agent wants a proper professional contract, or else “we’ll consider other offers”.

o.l: Renew with a raise right away
o.r: {player} signs happily: the talent stays home.

o.l: No blackmail: he has to earn it
o.r: {player} is disappointed. The agent storms out.

ch_teen_agent_offer.d: Just as the agent warned, a big club offers far more than {player}’s value ({value}).

o.l: Sell: an offer you can’t refuse
o.r: {player} leaves. A big fee comes in.

o.l: Match the wages and tie him down
o.r: A long contract and a starter’s salary: {player} stays.

o.l: Convince him to stay without money
o.r: {player} buys into the project: he stays and commits to the club.
o.rb: {player} feels held against his will and asks to leave.

ch_style_revolution.d: Your assistant proposes overhauling the way you play: new distances, new movements, two weeks of intense work.

o.r: The team starts from scratch on its principles. Patience needed.
Better automatisms, but the board expected a jolt.

ch_style_revolution_review.d: Five matchdays have passed since the tactical overhaul. Time to see if the team has absorbed it.

o.r: The players move by memory: the new football works.
o.rb: Too much confusion: half the team hasn’t understood the movements.

ch_ultras_tickets.d: The organised supporters ask the club to pay half the cost of away tickets.

o.r: The ultras say thanks with a banner. There’ll be plenty of them away from home.
The board approves. The ultras don’t.

ch_ultras_away_day.d: Thanks to the club-funded tickets, thousands of fans will travel. The police ask for guarantees.

o.r: A full, colourful away end: the team flies.
o.rb: Flares and clashes: a heavy fine and a furious board.

o.r: A quiet away day, disappointed fans.

ch_senior_feud.d: {player} and the captain came to blows in training. Everyone is looking at you.

o.r: The hierarchy holds. {player} won’t forget it.
{player} feels understood. The other senior players frown.

o.l: Lock them in a room until they make peace
o.r: They shake hands: the group comes out stronger.
o.rb: The peace is fake: the atmosphere stays heavy.

ch_senior_feud_after.d: After the fight with the captain, {player} trains apart and barely speaks.

o.l: Take him aside and clear the air
o.r: {player} appreciates it: the wound heals.
o.rb: {player} asks his agent to find him another club.

o.l: Leave him in the stands for a match
o.r: {player} gets the message, but the relationship cools.

ch_money_friendly.d: A sheikh offers €1.2 million for a friendly abroad during the international break.

o.r: Money in the bank, but twelve hours of flying in the legs.

o.l: Decline: the break is for resting
o.r: A rested team. The board gave up the money reluctantly.

ch_money_friendly_after.d: The team has just returned from the friendly abroad. The fitness coach fears jet lag.

o.r: The trip brought the group together, no consequences.
o.rb: Heavy legs and minds elsewhere: the team is tired.

o.r: Energy restored, some tactical work skipped.

ch_investor_visit.d: A foreign fund is considering buying into {club}. The chairman wants you to host the visit.

o.r: Half a day lost to work, but the investor is impressed.

o.l: I coach: the club can handle it
o.r: The squad appreciates it. The chairman much less.

ch_investor_decision.d: The foreign fund has made its decision about {club}. The chairman calls you in.

o.r: The fund buys in: more money for transfers and a more ambitious club.
o.rb: The fund pulls out. The chairman is in a foul mood.

ch_striker_backing.d: At the press conference you’re asked whether {player}, who hasn’t scored for weeks, is still the right man.

o.l: “He’ll score in the next three matches”
o.r: {player} thanks you with a look. But now the quote is in the papers.
{player} is hurt. The message reaches the whole group.

ch_striker_backing_verdict.d: Three matches have passed since you guaranteed goals from {player}. The journalists kept count.

o.r: {player} proved you right: the drought is over and the striker is reborn.
o.rb: {player} didn’t score: the quote backfires and he is devastated.

ch_keeper_rotation.d: {player} asks for game time: he is training well and wants at least a few matches.

o.l: Promise him two of the next five matches
o.r: {player} is beaming. Now you have to keep your word.
{player} accepts, but is disappointed.

ch_physio_method.d: A fitness coach proposes a data-driven injury prevention programme. It’s expensive, and results only show over time.

o.r: New sensors and new routines: we’ll see in a few weeks.
No changes.

ch_physio_method_result.d: The fitness coach presents the data from the last eight weeks.

o.r: Less fatigue and tougher muscles: the programme works.
o.rb: No improvement: the players complain about the extra routines.

dr_clans.d: In the canteen the players eat at separate tables by language. The group is splitting into cliques.

o.l: Mix up the rooms at training camp
o.r: Mixed rooms and group tasks: new friendships form.
o.rb: Forcing it annoys everyone: the cliques close up even more.

o.l: Organise a day out, all together
o.r: A day of go-karts and barbecue: the ice breaks.

o.l: Ask the senior players to sort it out
o.r: The seniors appreciate the trust, but the problem stays.

dr_late_arrival.d: {player} turns up late for the team coach: the whole squad waited twenty minutes for him.

o.l: He stays home: not called up
o.r: The message is clear to everyone.
The internal rules are applied, no drama.
{player} is grateful. The others notice the double standard.

dr_leaders_council.d: The most experienced players propose a “leadership group” to speak to you on behalf of everyone.

o.r: The group feels heard: the senior players become your allies.

o.l: I talk to everyone, one by one
o.r: No new structure.

dr_fasting.d: {player} observes a period of religious fasting and asks to adapt training and meal times.

o.r: {player} feels respected; a little less energy in the first weeks.
{player} follows the rules, but feels misunderstood.

dr_music_gym.d: In the gym young and old players argue about music: trap on one side, eighties rock on the other.

o.r: The kids cheer. The veterans cover their ears.
Pecking order respected. The youngsters sulk.
A seasoned manager’s solution: everyone’s happy.

dr_whatsapp_leak.d: Screenshots from the team chat end up online: heavy jokes about your training methods.

o.r: The leak is plugged, but the dressing room feels watched.

o.l: Laugh about it in front of everyone
o.r: Your irony defuses the row and the group laughs with you.
o.rb: The group realises nobody controls anything: more leaks coming.

dr_team_dinner.d: The captain proposes a midweek team dinner with families.

o.r: An evening that brings people together: the group comes out stronger.
Postponed.

dr_fines_system.d: Your assistant proposes an internal rulebook with fines for lateness, phones at meals and bookings for dissent.

o.r: Fewer silly bookings, even if some grumble.
No new rules.

dr_prank_gone_wrong.d: {player} filled a teammate’s car with water balloons. The teammate didn’t take it well.

o.l: One match out of the squad
o.r: The prank costs him, but peace returns.

o.l: A public apology and pizza for everyone
o.r: The punishment turns into a party.

dr_goal_celebration.d: The players invented a group goal celebration. The fans love it, opponents find it provocative.

o.r: The group has fun and feels united.
No risk of tension on the pitch.

dr_captain_challenge.d: {player} acts like the captain: leads the warm-up, talks to the referee. The current captain doesn’t like it.

o.r: {player} is the new captain. The old captain takes it very badly.

o.l: The armband is not up for debate
o.r: {player} has to take a step back.
A compromise: a clear hierarchy and {player} valued.

dr_heavy_defeat_meeting.d: The team arrives at the training ground heads down. How do you handle the restart?

o.r: Honest things are said: the team finds itself again.
o.rb: The meeting descends into mutual accusations.

o.r: Two days away: everyone returns fresher.
Better tactical understanding, but legs and morale suffer.

dr_senior_resents_youth.d: {player} has lost his place to a younger player. In training he goes in hard on the kid.

o.r: {player} calms down. But one start has to come.

o.l: Ask him to help the kid grow
o.r: {player} accepts the mentor role.
o.rb: {player} feels humiliated and poisons the atmosphere.

dr_team_building.d: The staff propose a two-day camp with a military unit: assault courses, a night in tents, team challenges.

o.r: A tough, wonderful experience: the group comes back tight-knit.
The team stays home to recover.

dr_bet_in_dressing.d: You discover {player} runs card games with real money at training camp. Some lost big sums.

o.r: The board approves. {player} is furious.
The problem seems solved, but word reaches the boardroom.

dr_birthday_coach.d: The players have prepared a birthday surprise: they want to start training an hour late.

o.r: Cake, songs and a lighter session: the group loves you.
Party postponed until after training.

dr_new_signing_hazing.d: New arrivals must sing standing on a chair at the team dinner, as tradition demands.

o.r: Laughter and applause: the newcomers join the group.
A quiet dinner.

dr_phone_ban.d: Your assistant notices the players are always on their phones, even in the dressing room before matches.

o.r: More focus, some grumbling.
The group appreciates the freedom.

dr_star_ego.d: {player} demands to take every set piece and complains when teammates don’t pass to him.

o.l: Confront him in front of the group
o.r: The confrontation makes him think: {player} plays for the team again.
o.rb: {player} feels attacked and withdraws.

o.r: {player} is satisfied. His teammates less so.

dr_religious_group.d: Some players ask for a small quiet room at the training ground to pray or meditate.

o.r: A simple gesture that makes everyone feel respected.
Request declined.

dr_substitutes_upset.d: The team is winning, but the reserves are unhappy: the same players always start.

o.r: The reserves feel involved. The team loses some rhythm.
The benchwarmers grumble.

dr_translator.d: {player} doesn’t yet understand the tactical instructions well and gets movements wrong.

o.r: {player} understands and feels looked after.
{player} keeps struggling.

dr_retirement_announce.d: {player} tells you this will be his last season. He’d like to tell his teammates.

o.r: The group wants to give him a send-off to remember.

o.l: Ask him to think again: offer another year
o.r: {player} agrees to stay, but the thought of retiring lingers.

dr_kit_man.d: The club’s long-serving kit man retires after thirty years. The players want to throw him a party.

o.r: A moving party: the club is a family.
A quiet farewell.

dr_injured_isolated.d: {player} has been injured for weeks and does his rehab alone. He feels forgotten.

o.l: Bring him to the bench and meetings
o.r: {player} feels part of the group again.
He recovers a little sooner, but lonelier.

dr_training_intensity.d: The fitness coach asks whether to increase training intensity at this stage of the season.

o.r: The team gets sharper, but arrives more tired on match day.

o.l: Ease off: it’s a long season
o.r: Fresh legs, a little less rhythm.

dr_youngster_cries.d: {player}, one of the youngest, is crying in the dressing room: he feels responsible for the defeat.

o.l: Hug him in front of everyone
o.r: {player} feels protected and supported.
The toughness hardens him.
o.rb: The kid withdraws into himself.

dr_players_vs_staff.d: The players complain about the fitness coach: sessions “pointless and too long”.

o.r: The group is grateful. The fitness coach feels undermined.
The staff are united. The players grumble.

dr_holiday_request.d: The players ask for three extra days off during the winter break.

o.r: Everyone returns happy and rested, if a little rusty.
A few long faces, but the work goes on.

dr_old_captain_speech.d: {player} wants to give a speech before the derby to remind the younger players what this match means.

o.r: Goosebumps in the dressing room: the team takes the field like a storm.
Clear-headed preparation, without over-hyping.

dr_social_media_fight.d: {player} replied with insults to a fan who criticised him on social media.

o.l: A fine and one match out
o.r: A clear sign of respect for the fans.
{player} appreciates it, but the fans wanted a signal.

dr_mentor_pairs.d: Your assistant proposes pairing each youngster with a veteran, including off the pitch.

o.r: The youngsters grow with an example to follow.
No change.

dr_players_meeting_coach.d: After three winless games the senior players ask for a meeting: they think the tactics are wrong.

o.r: The exchange is frank and constructive.
o.rb: Nobody convinces anybody: the rift widens.

o.r: The players feel heard, but the team loses some automatisms.
Authority reaffirmed. The group is cold.

dr_penalty_miss_consolation.d: {player} missed a decisive penalty and can’t forgive himself.

o.r: {player} feels backed and remains the penalty taker.
A cautious choice, but {player} is hurt.

dr_quiet_star.d: {player} is a star, but talks to nobody. The staff say you don’t really know what he thinks.

o.l: Invite him to lunch, just the two of you
o.r: You discover a sensitive person: your relationship changes.
Nothing changes.

dr_captains_armband_rotation.d: A youngster suggests rotating the captain’s armband in friendlies and cup games.

o.r: The youngsters love it, the seniors are puzzled.
Hierarchy intact.

dr_overconfidence.d: After three wins there’s too much joking and too little work in training.

o.r: The team refocuses.
The mood is great, but concentration drops.

dr_family_day.d: The captain proposes a training session open to the players’ partners, children and parents.

o.r: A day of smiles: the group becomes a family.
Work as usual.

dr_rival_friendship.t: The friend on the other team
dr_rival_friendship.d: Fans saw {player} having dinner with a player from the rival team on the eve of the derby.

o.l: Ask him to avoid such photos
o.r: {player} understands, though he finds it over the top.
{player} is grateful. The ultras disagree.

dr_substitute_tantrum.d: {player}, subbed off, refused your handshake and kicked a bottle towards the bench.

o.l: One match out and a public apology
o.r: The group sees rules apply to everyone.
{player} apologises sincerely.
o.rb: It goes unpunished and others feel entitled.

dr_training_game_bet.d: The reserves challenge the starters to a practice match: losers buy breakfast for a month.

o.r: A fierce, hilarious match: the reserves win, amid laughter.
A normal session.

fn_ultras_meeting.d: The ultras’ leaders ask for a meeting with the team and manager at the training ground after poor results.

o.r: You speak plainly and take responsibility: the fans respect it.
o.rb: The meeting gets heated: harsh words fly.

o.l: No meeting: the club doesn’t deal with ultras
o.r: The board approves. The ultras plan a protest.

o.l: Send the team to talk to them
o.r: The fans appreciate it, but some players come back shaken.

fn_training_protest.d: A group of fans turns up at the training ground gates chanting against the team.

o.r: The fans respect the courage, but the players suffer the jeers.

o.l: Train at a pitch far away
o.r: The team works in peace. The fans feel snubbed.

fn_kids_visit.d: Two hundred kids from the city’s football schools want to watch a training session and take photos with the players.

o.r: A morning of smiles: the city speaks well of the team.

o.l: Maybe at the end of the season
o.r: Postponed.

fn_away_heroes.t: In front of the away end
fn_away_heroes.d: After the away win the fans call team and manager over to the away end.

o.l: Everyone to the fans, shirts thrown in
o.r: A beautiful scene: the fans go home in love.

o.l: A quick wave and into the tunnel
o.r: A polite wave.

fn_chant_player.d: At the stadium {player} is jeered every time he touches the ball.

o.l: Ask the fans to support him
o.r: {player} feels protected. Some fans don’t like the lecture.

o.l: Take him out of the team for a while
o.r: The fans approve. {player} is crushed.

o.l: Keep him on: he has to react
o.r: {player} answers with a great performance.
o.rb: The jeers crush him.

fn_fan_favourite.d: The fans have made a banner asking for {player}, a fan favourite, to play.

o.r: The fans cheer. Now a start has to come.
Consistent, but the fans are disappointed.

fn_stadium_empty.d: At the last home game there were only ten thousand people. The club wants a letter to the fans signed by you.

o.r: The words touch the fans: they come back to the stadium.

o.l: The pitch will do the talking
o.r: The stadium stays half empty.

fn_choreography.d: The ultras prepare a giant display for the derby and ask the players to come out of the tunnel with you.

o.l: We all go out in front of the fans
o.r: Goosebumps: the team takes the field on a wave.

o.l: A normal warm-up, heads on the game
o.r: Focus, less emotion.

fn_crowdfunding.d: The fans organise a fundraiser to help the club buy a new signing.

o.r: Money comes in, and a special bond with the city.
The fans don’t understand the refusal.

fn_supporter_vote.d: The club proposes letting fans vote for player of the month on the official app, with an award on the pitch.

o.r: The fans take part in droves. Some in the dressing room count the votes.
No initiative.

fn_banner_coach.d: A banner appears at the stadium with your name: “A manager, a leader”.

o.r: An emotional moment: your name spreads everywhere.

o.l: Thank them, but the credit goes to the players
o.r: The players appreciate it.

fn_car_attack.d: After three defeats, some thugs damaged {player}’s car outside his home.

o.r: The team rallies around its teammate.
A cautious silence, but {player} feels alone.

fn_legend_return.d: A legendary former captain returns for a celebration. He wants to address the team before the match.

o.l: Yes, let him speak to the team
o.r: His words stay in the players’ heads.

o.l: Just a photo before the game
o.r: A low-key celebration.

fn_ticket_scandal.d: It emerges that {player} was reselling the club’s complimentary tickets at inflated prices.

o.l: Internal ban and apology to fans
o.r: The fans appreciate the firmness.
The story reaches the papers anyway.

fn_rain_match.d: In the match played in a downpour the fans never stopped singing. They’d like a gesture.

o.l: A double lap of honour in the rain
o.r: The fans love it: a stronger bond.
A small gesture.

fn_rival_fans_provocation.d: Rival fans hung a mocking banner outside your training ground.

o.r: The team is furious: fired up but edgy.
No distraction.

fn_fans_kit_design.d: The club proposes a contest: the fans will design the third kit.

o.r: Thousands of designs: the fans feel part of the club.
No contest.

fn_hospital_visit.d: A young fan in hospital dreams of meeting the team.

o.l: We all go to visit him
o.r: A day nobody will forget.
A nice gesture from afar.

fn_supporters_trust_style.d: The supporters’ association writes an open letter: the team plays too defensively.

o.r: The fans appreciate it; the team must adapt.
Consistent, but the stadium murmurs.

fn_pitch_invader_hug.d: A young boy ran onto the pitch to hug {player}. The stewards dragged him off roughly.

o.l: Invite the boy to the training ground
o.r: The gesture moves the city.
A strict stance.

fn_debt_protest.d: The fans protest: the club isn’t investing. They ask if the squad is good enough.

o.r: The fans agree with you. The board doesn’t.
The board appreciates the loyalty.

fn_anniversary.d: It’s the club’s anniversary: for the home match the team wears a historic kit.

o.l: A big party at the stadium
o.r: A magical atmosphere: the team feels part of history.
A low-key celebration.

fn_signing_request.d: The fans demand a marquee signing. A hashtag against the club trends online.

o.l: Ask the club for an effort
o.r: The fans feel you’re with them; part of the budget goes on a showpiece deal.
A firm stance, disappointed fans.

fn_minute_silence.d: A long-time club kit man has passed away. The fans ask for a special tribute.

o.l: Black armbands and a minute’s silence
o.r: A moment that unites team and city.
A quiet tribute.

fn_scarf_ban.d: The police ban flags and drums for safety reasons. The fans threaten to stay silent.

o.r: The ultras thank you.

o.l: Ask for rules to be respected
o.r: An institutional stance.

fn_fan_trains.d: A fan won a contest: to train with the team for a day.

o.l: Let him play in the practice match too
o.r: The fan scores amid everyone’s laughter: a viral video.
A calmer experience.

fn_old_rival_fans.d: At the victory celebration you’re handed a microphone in front of the fans. They want a joke about the old rivals.

o.r: The fans go wild. The rivals take note.
Class.

fn_player_fan_club.d: A fan club dedicated to {player} has been founded. They invite him to the launch party.

o.r: {player} is thrilled and the fans adore him.
{player} postpones, a little disappointed.

fn_empty_stadium_penalty.d: Because of discriminatory chants by a few, the judge has ordered a match behind closed doors. The club can appeal.

o.l: Appeal: don’t punish everyone for a few
o.r: The appeal fails and costs money, but the fans appreciate the fight.
The right stance, but the ultras feel punished.

fn_supporters_awards.d: The supporters’ clubs host their end-of-season dinner and invite you with the team.

o.r: A warm evening: fans and team embrace.
A token presence.

md_flu.d: A flu virus is going round: six players with a fever a few days before the match.

o.r: Some weakened players will have to play.
The spread stops earlier.

md_surgery_choice.d: The surgeon proposes operating on {player}: a longer lay-off, but the problem solved for good. Or conservative treatment.

o.r: {player} will be out longer, but return as good as new.
The treatment works: {player} is back soon.
o.rb: The treatment isn’t enough: a relapse, and the problem remains.

md_gps_warning.d: The GPS data say {player} is in the red zone: a very high risk of muscle injury.

o.r: {player} recovers: better one match out than a month.
He holds up and plays well.
o.rb: The muscle gives way: a strain.

md_second_opinion.d: {player}’s agent asks for a second medical opinion abroad: he doesn’t trust the club’s diagnosis.

o.r: The second doctor shortens the recovery time.
o.rb: The second opinion confirms the first: time and money lost.

o.r: The staff appreciate it. The agent less so.

md_heat_wave.d: Forty degrees: the staff suggest moving training to dawn and evening.

o.r: The team suffers less from the heat.

o.l: Normal hours: they’ll get used to it
o.r: Heavy sessions, drained legs.

md_sleep_specialist.d: A sleep specialist proposes a programme for the team: routines, dark rooms, no screens at night.

o.r: The players sleep better and recover more.
No programme.

md_rushed_return.d: {player} wants to return right away: he says he feels fine. The medical staff advise caution.

o.l: Put him on the bench next match
o.r: {player} returns and is fine.
o.rb: A relapse: back to square one.

o.r: {player} is restless, but he’ll return at a hundred per cent.

md_painkillers.d: {player} lives with chronic pain and asks for painkillers before every match.

o.r: {player} plays better, but his body wears down.
{player} misses a few sessions and feels better.

md_bad_pitch_injuries.d: The medical staff suspect the worn training pitch is causing injuries.

o.r: A necessary expense: fewer knocks.

o.l: Wait until the end of the season
o.r: The pitch stays as it is.

md_concussion.d: In training {player} took a knock to the head. He says he’s fine, but protocol requires rest.

o.r: {player} misses one match to be safe.
No consequences.
o.rb: The symptoms return during the match: a longer lay-off and controversy.

md_new_physio_method.d: A physio proposes an experimental muscle recovery method.

o.r: It works: the players recover faster.
o.rb: It doesn’t work and wastes time.

o.r: No change.

md_ankle_brace.d: The staff want {player} to play with a rigid ankle brace after past sprains. He says it takes away his feel.

o.r: Less risk, a little less agility.
No change.

md_travel_fatigue.d: Tests show general fatigue. The fitness coach proposes a recovery week.

o.r: The team regenerates.
Better understanding, less energy.

md_old_injury_flare.d: An old knee problem has flared up for {player}.

o.l: Two matches out as a precaution
o.r: Rest, and the knee settles.
The knee holds up.
o.rb: The knee gives way: a long lay-off.

md_doping_test.d: A surprise doping control at the training ground at six in the morning: it’s {player}’s turn, and he was ill during the night.

o.r: {player} appreciates the support. All clear.
All clear, but {player} feels alone.

md_food_poisoning.d: After dinner at the away hotel many players are ill.

o.r: A weakened team takes the field.

o.l: Doctor, drips and rest until the last minute
o.r: The team partly recovers.

md_mental_fatigue.d: The staff psychologist reports that {player} is mentally exhausted.

o.r: {player} returns at peace.
{player} gets worse.

md_blood_tests.d: The staff propose monthly blood tests to tailor each player’s diet and supplements.

o.r: Tailored plans: the team benefits.
No change.

md_hamstring_epidemic.d: The medical staff link the muscle injuries to your demanding style of play.

o.l: Lower the intensity for a few weeks
o.r: Fewer injuries, but the play loses intensity.
No change: muscles keep suffering.

md_young_growth.d: {player} has grown seven centimetres in a year: the staff want to reduce his loads to protect his joints.

o.r: {player} trains less, but grows up healthy.
{player} trains with everyone, with some risk.

md_keeper_finger.d: {player} dislocated a finger in training. He can play strapped up, but it’s risky.

o.r: The back-up keeper plays.
He grits his teeth and holds up.
o.rb: The finger can’t take it: a longer lay-off.

md_altitude.d: The fitness coach proposes a ten-day altitude camp to boost endurance.

o.r: Endurance improved for months.
No change.

md_physio_leak.d: {player}’s diagnosis reached the papers before the club announced it.

o.r: The staff shrinks, the board’s trust grows.
Will it happen again?

md_ice_bath_refusal.d: {player} refuses to take ice baths after training: “I hate it”.

o.r: {player} complies, grumbling, and recovers better.
{player} recovers worse.

md_marathon_run.d: The city organises a charity run and asks the team to take part.

o.r: A good image and a united group, slightly tired legs.
The team rests.

md_knee_scan.d: {player} feels a niggle in his knee. A scan would mean a precautionary week off.

o.r: Nothing serious: {player} returns rested.
The niggle goes away.
o.rb: It was serious: out.

md_vitamin_drip.d: The doctor proposes vitamin drips before matches. All legal, but in the papers it might look like something else.

o.r: Some benefit, and some snide press.
No image risk.

md_mouthguard.d: After an aerial challenge {player} lost a tooth. The doctor wants him to play with a mouthguard.

o.r: {player} grumbles, but he’s better protected.
No mouthguard.

md_rehab_abroad.d: {player} wants to do his rehab at a specialist centre in his home country.

o.r: A slightly faster recovery, but {player} drifts from the group.
{player} stays close to the team.

pl_extra_training.d: The coaching staff propose an extra training plan for {player}: afternoons in the gym and video of his matches. It could be the leap forward, or it could burn him out.

o.r: {player} responds superbly: more confident, sharper, quicker in thought.
o.rb: {player} can’t take it: he drags himself around, complains and ends up with a strain.

o.r: {player} appreciates the trust and trains calmly.

pl_bench_star.d: {player} is one of the best in the squad, but lately he has the lowest average rating in the team. The papers want him dropped.

o.l: Drop him for a match to shake him up
o.r: Being dropped stings: he’s a different man in training and returns hungry.
o.rb: {player} takes it as a humiliation and stops talking to you.

o.l: He starts, trust is not up for debate
o.r: {player} thanks you and promises to repay you.

o.l: Defend him at the press conference
o.r: The gesture fires him up, but some in the dressing room think different rules apply to him.

pl_position_change_fb.d: The staff see a modern full-back in {player}: running, crossing, one against one. But he has always seen himself as an attacker.

o.l: Try him at full-back right away
o.r: Experiment works: {player} finds a new role and thrives in it.
o.rb: {player} plays full-back reluctantly: he learns to defend, but loses his smile.

o.r: {player} carries on in his role.

pl_position_change_mid.d: In training {player} builds play better than many midfielders. What if he became your holding midfielder?

o.l: Yes, move him to holding midfield
o.r: {player} dictates the tempo as if he had always done it.
o.rb: In midfield {player} struggles: the pace is different.

o.r: Everything stays as it is.

pl_striker_to_wing.d: With plenty of strikers in the squad, the staff suggest moving {player} out wide, where he can run at people.

o.r: {player} loves it: dribbles, crosses, goals from wide.
o.rb: {player} gets lost on the flank: he never receives the ball where he wants it.

o.r: {player} stays at the centre of the attack.

pl_captaincy.d: The dressing room wonders who should wear the armband. {player} doesn’t say it, but he hopes.

o.r: {player} becomes the captain the team needed: he talks, drives, protects the youngsters.
o.rb: {player} takes the armband, but the senior players don’t accept him as their leader.

o.r: {player} is disappointed, but understands.

pl_promise_minutes.d: {player} walks into your office: he’s barely playing and wants to know what future he has at this club.

o.l: Promise him three starts in the next six matches
o.r: {player} leaves the office walking taller. Now the promise has to be kept.

o.l: Tell him to earn his place in training
o.r: {player} takes up the challenge and goes all out in training.
o.rb: {player} hears only a no, and his mood collapses.

o.l: Remind him that I make the decisions
o.r: The door closes quickly. The board likes the firmness, he likes it far less.

promise_kept.d: You gave {player} the matches you promised: {count} starts out of {need}. He won’t forget it.

o.r: {player} would now run through walls for you.

promise_broken.d: You promised {player} {need} starts. He got {count}. The dressing room saw everything.

o.r: {player} tells his agent he wants out.

o.l: Apologise to him in front of everyone
o.r: The public apology mends things a little: {player} gives you another chance.
o.rb: The apology comes too late: {player} takes it as mockery and the dressing room splits.

pl_transfer_request.d: {player}’s agent has submitted a formal transfer request. Estimated value: {value} million.

o.l: Sell him to the highest bidder
o.r: {player} leaves. Money comes in, a problem walks out of the dressing room.

o.l: Keep him and try to patch things up
o.r: A dinner, a real heart-to-heart: {player} stays and is back on your side.
o.rb: {player} stays against his will and it shows: lazy sessions, long faces.

o.l: Loan him out until the end of the season
o.r: {player} goes to play elsewhere. He’ll be back, maybe better.

pl_night_out.d: Photos of {player} at three in the morning in a club, two days before the match. They’re already all over social media.

o.l: Fine him and drop him for a match
o.r: The message reaches everyone: rules apply to all.
{player} pays the fine. On the pitch, though, his legs are heavy.

o.l: Turn a blind eye, talk to him privately
o.r: The show of trust wins him over: he never steps out of line again.
o.rb: {player} does it again the next week, and this time everyone finds out.

pl_play_hurt.d: {player} is injured but wants to play with a painkilling injection. The doctor isn’t convinced.

o.r: {player} grits his teeth and holds up: a warrior’s performance.
o.rb: The pain worsens on the pitch: now he’ll be out much longer.

o.r: The doctor approves. {player} is restless, but recovers without risk.

pl_young_debut.d: {player} is eighteen and dazzling in training. The staff say he’s ready for his debut.

o.l: Throw him in from the start
o.r: {player} plays with the nerve of a veteran. Is a star being born?
o.rb: The pressure crushes him: he gets everything wrong and leaves in tears.

o.l: Wait, he needs to grow calmly
o.r: {player} keeps working away from the spotlight.

pl_renewal_star.d: {player}’s contract expires at the end of the season. His agent wants a big raise.

o.r: He signs for four years: {player} is the face of the project.
{player} accepts: he wants to stay more than he wants the money.
o.rb: {player} feels undervalued: he’ll leave on a free.

o.r: The club saves money, but in June {player} will say goodbye.

pl_renewal_veteran.d: {player} is one of the veterans. He’d like to finish his career here, with a one-year deal.

o.r: {player} thanks you, moved: the dressing room appreciates the respect shown to veterans.

o.l: Two years and a small raise
o.r: {player} signs happily. The board frowns a little.
At the end of the season {player} will leave the club.

pl_diet_program.d: The nutritionist says {player} is carrying a few extra kilos and proposes a strict diet with conditioning work.

o.r: Two months later {player} is flying: more stamina, fewer knocks.
o.rb: {player} hates the diet and stops following it. And he blames you.

o.r: No change to {player}’s routine.

pl_psychologist.t: {player} is not in a good place
pl_psychologist.d: {player} has been down for weeks. In training he gets simple things wrong and keeps to himself.

o.l: Send him to the mental coach
o.r: A few sessions and {player} gets his head back: calmer in the moments that matter.
o.rb: {player} sees the mental coach as a vote of no confidence.

o.l: I’ll talk to him, man to man
o.r: An hour-long chat: {player} walks out relieved.

o.l: He has to react on his own
o.r: The board likes the tough line. {player} keeps struggling.

pl_free_kick_specialist.t: A hundred free kicks a day
pl_free_kick_specialist.d: {player} stays after training to practise free kicks. He asks for a dedicated coach.

o.r: {player} sharpens his technique: a free kick on the edge is now a weapon.
o.rb: Too many kicks, too much strain: {player} is out with an adductor problem.

o.r: {player} goes back to group training.

pl_agent_rumours.d: {player}’s agent is spreading rumours about a big club’s interest. Estimated value: {value} million.

o.l: Call him and ask him to stay focused
o.r: {player} assures you he wants to stay: the rumour fades.
o.rb: {player} wavers: his head is already elsewhere.

o.r: The board digs in. {player} doesn’t take it too well.
The fans cheer and {player} appreciates the stance.

pl_big_offer.d: A top club offers 30% above {player}’s value ({value} million). The board leaves the final word to you.

o.r: {player} leaves, the coffers fill up. The fans don’t take it well.
{player} would have liked to discuss it. The fans, though, love you.

o.l: Refuse and offer a new contract
o.r: {player} signs long term and becomes a club icon.
o.rb: {player} wanted to go and the new deal isn’t enough: he’s furious.

pl_loan_youngster.d: A lower-division club wants {player} on loan and guarantees him a starting place.

o.r: Great call: {player} plays every weekend and grows before your eyes.
o.rb: The loan is a disaster: the bench and a coach who doesn’t rate him.

o.l: He stays and trains with the first team
o.r: {player} stays, but he won’t see many minutes.

o.l: He stays and I promise him chances
o.r: {player} is thrilled. Now he really needs two starts.

pl_hothead.d: {player} came to blows with a teammate during a practice match. The dressing room waits for your reaction.

o.l: Banished from the squad for two matches
o.r: An iron fist: the group approves, {player} much less.

o.l: Lock them in a room until they sort it out
o.r: They come out hugging: the fight becomes a friendship.
o.rb: They come out even angrier and the dressing room splits in two.

o.r: {player} is sold: the problem is gone, and some quality with it.

pl_hat_trick_hero.d: {player} is the man of the moment: front pages, interviews, ads. Do you leave him in the spotlight?

o.r: {player} enjoys the moment and keeps scoring.
o.rb: Too much exposure: {player} loses focus and fades.

o.r: {player} understands: head down and work.

pl_veteran_mentor.t: {player} takes the youngsters under his wing
pl_veteran_mentor.d: {player} offers to mentor the youngest players after training. The staff agree.

o.l: Yes, he looks after the kids
o.r: The youngsters hang on {player}’s every word: they develop faster.

o.l: I’d rather he focuses on himself
o.r: {player} concentrates on his own work and benefits from it.

pl_homesick.d: {player} is struggling to settle: far from family, a new language, few friends.

o.r: {player} returns refreshed, even if he missed a few sessions.

o.l: He has to get used to it, it’s part of the job
o.r: {player} rolls up his sleeves and makes it.
o.rb: {player} withdraws even more and it shows on the pitch.

o.l: The club pays for a teacher and a tutor
o.r: Small gestures that make a difference: {player} feels at home.

pl_contract_clause.d: Several clubs are watching {player}. The board suggests tying him down with a long contract and a high release clause.

o.r: {player} signs and thanks you. He’s the club’s future.

o.l: Not now, let’s see how he develops
o.r: {player} expected more consideration.

pl_style_misfit.d: {player} is struggling in your playing style and tells you plainly: he can’t perform like this.

o.l: Convince him to work on adapting
o.r: {player} gives it everything: now he looks made for this football.
o.rb: {player} can’t find his feet and frustration grows.

o.r: {player} comes alive, but the team loses some of its automatisms.
The group respects the consistency. {player} doesn’t.

pl_penalty_argument.d: {player} wants to be the penalty taker and makes sure everyone knows it, including the current taker.

o.r: {player} takes responsibility and doesn’t flinch.
o.rb: The decision causes friction with the former taker.

o.r: {player} goes along with it. The group likes that the rules stay the same.

pl_charity.d: {player} wants to attend a charity event at the city’s children’s hospital, the day before an important training session.

o.r: The photos go around the city: fans are moved and {player} is happy.
{player} postpones, a little disappointed.

pl_social_post.d: After the defeat {player} posts a pointed story: “Those who play don’t deserve it, those who deserve it don’t play”.

o.r: The dressing room understands some things are not done.
{player} deletes the post and apologises to his teammates.
o.rb: The talk isn’t enough: the post becomes a national story.

o.r: The row blows over, but the fans grumble.

pl_injury_prone_plan.d: The medical staff fear {player}’s body is at risk and propose a prevention plan with reduced workloads.

o.r: A few weeks at reduced pace, but {player} is now at much lower risk.

o.l: No plan, we need him on the pitch
o.r: {player} carries on at full tilt. Let’s hope he holds up.

pl_comeback_slow.d: A specialist abroad proposes an experimental therapy to speed up {player}’s recovery.

o.r: It works: {player} returns ahead of schedule and stronger.
o.rb: The therapy fails: recovery takes longer.

o.r: {player} recovers calmly and returns without after-effects.

pl_role_model_kid.d: The scouts say {player} has the potential to become a star. Do you give him a personal programme?

o.r: {player} grows protected and motivated. A few senior players frown.
{player} follows the same path as everyone else.

pl_gk_distribution.t: The keeper has to play with his feet

pl_super_sub.d: {player} scores as soon as he comes on. Now he wants a starting shirt.

p2_fitness_test_cheat.d: The fitness coach discovers {player} cut the course during the endurance tests.

p2_mentor_promise.d: {player} asks what he needs to do to play. He’s young and hungry.

p2_captain_injury_leader.d: {player} is injured but wants to sit on the bench during matches to lead his teammates.

He recovers a touch sooner.

p2_goalkeeper_rivalry.d: {player}, the second goalkeeper, asks to compete for the spot: in training he saves everything.

{player} stays number two, disappointed.
The contest fires him up.

p2_hidden_injury.d: The physio tells you {player} is hiding pain so he won’t lose his place.

The trust unlocks him.

p2_leader_emerges.d: {player} is becoming a reference point for his teammates. The staff suggest giving him more responsibility.

o.r: {player} matures: more confident on and off the pitch.
No change.

p2_weak_foot_striker.d: Your assistant notices {player} always shoots the same way: keepers have studied him.

o.r: {player} becomes unpredictable in front of goal.

o.r: No extra work.

p2_playmaker_freedom.d: {player} asks for freedom to roam wherever he likes, with no covering duties.

An organised team, a less happy {player}.

p2_old_player_role.d: {player}’s legs aren’t what they were. The staff suggest moving him more centrally.

o.l: Turn him into an attacking playmaker
o.r: {player} reinvents himself: brains instead of legs.
o.rb: {player} won’t accept the new role.

o.l: He stays in his role while he can
o.r: No change.

p2_injury_prone_star.d: The medical staff propose resting {player} one match in five to preserve him.

{player} always on the pitch.

p2_player_religion_match.d: For {player} an important religious holiday falls on match day: he asks to join the team hotel later.

o.r: {player} appreciates the respect.
{player} complies, reluctantly.

p2_contract_bonus.d: {player} is two appearances from a contract bonus. The chairman quietly asks you not to play him.

o.l: He plays if he deserves it
o.r: {player} earns the bonus: respect gained.
The club saves money. {player} understands everything and won’t forgive.

p2_protected_star_press.t: The young star and the pressure
p2_protected_star_press.d: {player} is very young and already among the best. Everyone wants a piece of him.

o.l: Shield him from media and sponsors
o.r: He grows up calmly.
Popularity and sponsors, some distraction.

p2_training_fight_star.d: In a practice match {player} made a vicious tackle on a youngster, out of frustration.

o.r: The group sees the law is equal for all.

o.l: Turn a blind eye: we need him

p2_mental_block_penalty.t: The mental block in front of goal
p2_mental_block_penalty.d: {player} is afraid of missing when one-on-one. The mental coach proposes visualisation exercises.

o.r: {player} regains his composure.

p2_ex_club_return.d: Against {opponent} {player} faces the club that discarded him. He wants to play at all costs.

A cautious choice, {player} disappointed.

p2_player_studies.d: {player} wants to start his coaching badges. He asks to sit in on your tactical meetings.

o.r: No change.

p2_homesick_again.d: {player} never settled: he asks to return to his country, even on loan.

o.r: {player} finds peace again.
{player} leaves, happy.

p2_captain_old_new.d: {player}, the captain, is 33 and plays less and less. The group wonders who the next captain will be.

o.l: Ask him to choose his successor
o.r: {player} accepts with dignity and names an heir.

o.l: While he’s in the squad, he’s captain
o.r: {player} is grateful.

p2_player_speed_record.d: GPS data show {player} is the fastest player in the league. The club wants to make a video.

o.r: {player} is proud and even more motivated.
No video.

p2_defender_leadership.d: {player} wants to lead the back line: calling offside, organising marking.

o.r: A tidier defence and a more responsible {player}.

o.r: No change.

p2_player_diet_fail.d: After the holidays {player} returned three kilos heavier.
